review_context: Round-2 re-review after the author addressed reviewer2 FIX_REQUIRED items. No LaTeX files were modified.
verdict_summary: The prior blocking issues are adequately addressed. The manuscript now qualifies the mixed third-set design in the abstract/method, defines the scenario-to-framework mapping, makes cost provenance explicit, and expands validity threats to include content-inclusion scoring, non-blinded local review, lack of confidence intervals/significance tests, and model/pricing instability. The main numerical tables still match the current 23-chain final artifacts. I would not require another blocking revision on correctness or traceability grounds.

legacy27_filtered_third_set_qualificatio.evidence: The abstract now says each model has 207 scored rows and that the third structured-model set is a legacy 27-chain run filtered to the current 23-chain scope. The method section also says the 4.1/5.4 third set is not a fresh formal23 replicate but a legacy27-filtered practical third set.

scenario_framework_mapping.evidence: The data/scenario description and scenario-result paragraph now map explicit_execution_chain to network_service_behavior plus command_shell_execution, multi_step_tool_chain to collection_or_tool_invocation plus script_execution_chain, and semantic_interpretation_chain to persistence_registry_run_key. The semantic group is also explicitly limited to one chain / nine scored rows.

cost_provenance.evidence: The cost paragraph and caption now distinguish 4.1/5.4 local ledger/local price estimates from the GPT-5.5 token/progress-side reconstructed estimate. The GPT-5.5 caveat says the figure is not an invoice amount.

limitations_strength.evidence: The threats-to-validity section now includes single-environment scope, mixed third-set source, raw-output salvage, Stage 3 retaining EDR telemetry, content-inclusion component-rubric judgment, non-blinded local review, no confidence intervals/significance tests over 23 chains, and model/pricing instability.

numerical_consistency.overall_table: pass: main.tex values match results_23chain_20260614/overall.csv for all three models.
numerical_consistency.cost_table: pass with caveat: 4.1/5.4 rows match cost_effectiveness_by_model.csv; GPT-5.5 total $93.52 matches the cost audit note, and /evidence and /order are consistent with 530 evidence hits and 328 order hits.

interpretation_assessment.stage_interpretation: defensible; the text repeatedly states Stage 3 hides alert-summary rows but retains CBC EDR/NGAV and OS telemetry.
interpretation_assessment.scenario_interpretation: defensible; explicit chains are framed as easiest only for stronger models, and the semantic group is no longer overgeneralized.
interpretation_assessment.model_interpretation: defensible; GPT-5.5 low raw is presented as salvage / potential upper bound, not deployment-equivalent to structured models.
interpretation_assessment.cost_interpretation: defensible; the manuscript no longer treats mixed cost sources as equal invoice-quality totals.

non_blocking_notes: For final polish, consider keeping the exact phrase 'gpt-5.5 low raw' consistent everywhere, since the result artifacts use that label.
The cost table remains an estimate table, not an invoice table; the current caption and prose are adequate, but a footnote to the audit file would further help reproducibility if the venue allows it.
The conclusion still says Stage 3 shows alert-summary rows are not the only reconstruction path; this is acceptable because the abstract and discussion now qualify retained EDR/OS telemetry.
professor_review_bottom_line: OK. The revised manuscript is numerically consistent with the current 23-chain results and now makes the main methodological caveats explicit enough for submission-level review.
